smell_validity.evidence: Retired pipeline stages sit permanently behind fixed-false const switches across three crates, each dead predecessor living inside the same function as its replacement, served by orphaned private helpers and expired-rationale switch docs. The alternates (count-based trimming, prose tool listings, alias formatting) are genuine retired functionality, not filler; the cost and the boundary from runtime config and intentional public API are unmistakable.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Central functions now carry shadow implementations beside the live ones, so every reader must hand-fold constants to learn actual behavior, and every future edit must consciously ignore the disabled sibling to avoid drift. The switch module's expired-rationale docs actively misinform maintainers. Removing restores single-path ownership of each behavior, though not an architecture-level boundary.

development_plausibility.evidence: The two-move migration story fits this repository: prose-to-YAML tool formats, budget-versus-count trimming, and pre-1.0 namespaced model names mirror real LLM-domain transitions, and local const toggles beside consumers are idiomatic Rust. However, one guard of each shape (plain, negated, derived, true-constant, short-circuit) appears exactly once — an authored regularity revealing task design.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The prompt decisively fences every realistic near-miss: flipping switches is rejected as behavior-changing wrong direction, constants must be resolved from source rather than assumed, and orphaned switches, helpers and the switch module must not remain, preventing incomplete cleanup. Deprecated variants, the runtime budget override, and llama.cpp crates are excluded, preventing irrelevant redesign, while per-site edits stay unprescribed.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Eleven clusters serve distinct purposes — conversation trimming, tool listing, token splitting, fence parsing, stream assembly, prompt combining, model naming, role mapping, token accounting, embeddings, mock echo — each requiring a code-supported decision: dead-side orientation varies (false, true, negated derived), the short-circuit site needs whole-branch deletion rather than side selection, helper and module cleanup differ by cluster.

localization_burden.evidence: The switch module's doc comments hand-link the core guard sites, and the prompt names affected subsystems and the locally declared toggles. Finding every site still takes several steps — module discovery, per-constant usage search, sibling-crate scan where one constant named for the unified scheme evades a legacy-named search — yet each site is classified within its own file without combining components' behavior.

repair_coordination.evidence: Two rules interlock: removing a guard orphans its helper and use-statements, and retiring constants must respect the derived pipeline constant, which itself references two stage switches — removing a stage constant first breaks compilation. Deletion extent at the short-circuit and adjacent-override sites is constrained by reachability analysis of the same condition, so edits cannot be independent.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: One uniform rule — resolve each compile-time constant, delete the permanently unreachable region, then sweep orphaned helpers, switches, imports and the switch module — covers all eleven guard sites and their machinery, over 80%, with behavior preserved by construction. Guard shapes differ syntactically but require no separate behavioral decision at any location.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Concrete wrong edits — enabling a disabled path, deleting the live side at the true-valued switch, or removing the adjacent environment override — compile and pass ordinary calls, diverging only in special state: over-budget conversations, name-bearing messages, short mock prompts, or the environment variable being set. No test evidence appears, so the unchecked-failure levels are not supported.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
